entry.title: Taskbar Volume Percentage Indicator 1.9.0
entry.content:
• Added separate vertical offset settings (verticalOffset and iconVerticalOffset) for the percentage text and native volume/mute icons to allow fine-tuned alignment.
  • Preserved stock and custom container margins when vertical offsets are set to zero.

entry.title: Desktop Window Cards 1.8
entry.content:
• New: hold a modifier key (Shift, Ctrl or Alt) while minimizing to send the window to the taskbar without a card.
  • New: option to invert the modifier key, so that only windows minimized while holding it become cards.
  • New: exclusion list of programs whose windows never become cards.

entry.title: CoverTabby 0.22.14
entry.content:
CoverTabby

Replaces the alt+tab with a modded kind of the stardock alt tabby's layout.

By LTHC (LoreTheHolyChip). Version 0.22.14.

Win+Tab integration is experimental and disabled by default. Alt+Tab remains enabled. Explorer forwards Alt+Tab to the switcher running in Windhawk’s own tool process. No separate application needs to be installed.

Credits: caliberda (MIT-licensed Alt+Tab Flip 3D renderer), Lone (touchpad integration), and the Simple Window Switcher contributors (HID parsing). Renderer: https://github.com/ramensoftware/windhawk-mods/blob/main/mods/alt-tab-flip-3d.wh.cpp Touchpad source by Lone (Louis047): https://github.com/ramensoftware/windhawk-mods/pull/5396 Simple Window Switcher credits the GPLv2 upstream sws by valinet: https://github.com/valinet/sws CoverTabby is distributed under GPL-2.0-only; MIT terms remain applicable to the renderer portions. License texts are included below in the source.

Styles

| Style | Preview | | --- | --- | | Tiles — Windowed | | | Tiles — Fullscreen | | | Normal — Windowed | | | Normal — Fullscreen | | | Icons only | | | No thumbnail | | | Text only | | | Search | | | Windows 10/11 Enchanted | |

These screenshots were captured using a macro. The same macro can generate fresh screenshots whenever I update CoverTabby.

thanks for using my mod :D

Windows 11 supported; Windows 10 1607 (build 14393) and newer are experimental and use the built-in Segoe MDL2 Assets icon font. On Windows 10 builds earlier than 20348, live-captured windows can display a yellow capture border because those builds cannot disable it. The desktop overview's virtual-desktop management requires Windows 11; on Windows 10, those controls are unavailable.

Pressing the top grip quickly reveals the real window without starting a drag. Move while holding to drag it with its native decorations and a short centered popup animation. Resizable windows shrink to the preview size while the remaining interface fades out. Releasing the mouse stops the drag. A simple click still switches windows. Canceling before dragging restores the window's original size, position and minimized/maximized state. Minimized and maximized windows are restored to a movable window before the drag begins, including minimized windows that would normally restore maximized. Drag from the top area of a preview: a standard Windows title bar or system menu is not required. Clicking elsewhere selects the window. Custom title bars and borderless application windows keep their own decorations. Fixed-size windows keep their native size while moving. Minimized windows show a card matching the Windows light/dark theme, with a top drag grip and a restore hint. The app icon remains in the icon strip below. If CoverTabby previously captured the window, its last preview is kept in memory and shown blurred and darkened while minimized. Holding the top grip reveals the restored real window with sharp content; moving starts the held drag. Windows without a saved preview use the regular theme-colored minimized card.

Modes

  • Full fills the monitor. Background Style chooses Blur, Opaque or Transparent.
  • Windowed uses a compact centered popup. Windowed Scale resizes the entire popup.

Colors, fonts and rounded corners follow Windows 11 automatically.

Enable Show Desktop Card to keep a Desktop item at the end of the carousel. Selecting it uses Windows' native Show Desktop action.

Language

Language is detected at every start: Italian for an Italian Windows display language, English otherwise. Window titles and custom desktop names keep their original text.

Features

Live previews, application icons, grouped windows, Pin / Unpin, hover close controls, reflections and smooth animations. Settings cover only the essentials. Hover Behavior offers Show Title, Select Window or None for unselected windows. Opening uses a quick stationary fade. On normal selection, the selected preview smoothly resizes and returns to the real window position, starting fast and slowing down at the end. The real window remains visible beneath the topmost overlay throughout this return animation. The background fades in place while the remaining previews, icons and controls slide down and fade. Dragging keeps following the mouse instead. Hover Animation offers None, Lift, Enlarge or Lift + Enlarge. It is disabled for unselected windows when Hover Behavior is None. Click a preview to activate it.

Search

While CoverTabby is open, press Alt+S, type a window title or application name, then press Enter. Search Bar Scale changes the bar, icon and text together. Width adapts automatically. Disable Search Bar to remove its reserved space and center the content. Search is unavailable in Windowed mode and Tiles.

Virtual desktops

In the Win+Tab overview, desktop cards include the Windows taskbar on the current desktop when capture is available, with a themed app bar as the fallback on that desktop only. Other desktops do not show a taskbar. A left-side app dock offers animated selection and hover labels; minimized windows use the separate upper dock. Desktop rename keeps the text caret and animates new letters with a quick fade, upward overshoot and smooth settling. Drag an app preview or dock icon onto another desktop card to move the window there, keeping its original position and size. A simple click activates it. Drag it away from the desktop cards to take the real window onto the current desktop. Maximized and minimized windows stay unchanged until movement begins, then restore to their normal size and follow the held pointer.

Hover the selected preview to reveal the green desktop icon and label alongside Pin and Close. Click it to open CoverTabby's own desktop picker, then choose a desktop to move the window there without changing its position or size. The current desktop stays active. Use the mouse wheel to scroll the list when there are many desktops.

Process information

CPU, RAM and GPU appear below the selected application's icon and refresh approximately every 1.5 seconds while the selection is stable. These are metrics for the process owning the selected window, not its child processes. RAM shows the working set in MB/GB; its color uses the percentage of physical RAM. GPU reports the busiest GPU engine for that process, or N/A when counters are unavailable. Usage colors are green up to 10%, white below 35%, yellow below 50%, orange up to 75%, and red above 75%. Hover the selected preview to see relative process age at the top right, such as Opened 5 minutes ago. This is process age, not window age. The skull button beside Close kills the owning process, including its other windows, after a second confirming click within four seconds. Unsaved work will be lost. Close continues to request normal application closure.

Icon controls

Hover an app icon for a small smooth lift, zoom and Windows accent background. Right-click an icon or preview to open CoverTabby's animated menu: Close, Kill, and Pin/Unpin. These actions target the clicked window without changing selection. Click outside or press Escape to dismiss. Releasing Alt still closes CoverTabby. The menu is rendered by CoverTabby and uses Segoe Fluent Icons.

Navigation

Alt+Tab cycles forward; Shift+Alt+Tab or Alt+` cycles backward. The first press selects the next or previous window relative to the active window, including when pinned windows change the list order. With Group Windows enabled, Up/Down selects a window in the current application. Windows from the same application stay consecutive. Switching between them moves the stack vertically; Left/Right changes applications horizontally. Mouse selection and wheel navigation are also supported.

Performance and background

Background Style offers Blur, Opaque and Transparent in Full and Windowed. Transparent Background Opacity controls the tint without applying blur. Background During Energy Saver automatically switches to Opaque or Transparent while Windows saves energy; Keep Selected Background disables this override.

The selected preview starts first. Other live previews start progressively, and opening waits at most 45 ms for the selected capture after startup. Desktop blur is captured at up to 960 pixels on its longest side. Preview Cache reuses up to twelve 512-pixel snapshots (384 during Energy Saver), updated gradually only while the switcher is open. When closed, captures stop except for a window currently being held and dragged. Dragging, search, groups, controls and animations remain available. VSync is always enabled: the render loop waits on DXGI frame availability with a one-frame queue and has no fixed 60 FPS cap. The actual rate follows the display compositor and available GPU performance.

Precision touchpad

Three fingers starting in the lower third and moving upward open CoverTabby. Continuing that same stroke sideways navigates. Starting in the middle third and moving upward requests normal closure of the selected window while CoverTabby is open. Swipe downward to dismiss; a short three-finger tap selects the current window. Holding still gives animated press feedback. Existing touchpad mouse-click/hold dragging stays available.

Touchpad from Modern Window Switcher — Lone. HID parsing adapted from the downloaded Simple Window Switcher 3.0 source. The gesture controller is used where supported; older Windows builds may require setting native three-finger swipe/tap actions to Nothing in Windows touchpad settings to prevent duplicate system actions. Disable Precision Touchpad Gestures to stop listening to touchpad reports.

Desktop overview

Hold to Preview is optional and disabled by default. In thumbnail styles, hold Alt on the same selection for five seconds to enlarge its native-resolution live capture to fit the monitor without stretching. Tab slides the enlarged image left; releasing Alt returns it toward the real window. Minimized previews also enlarge; two seconds after reaching full size, their minimized message changes to a playful message.

While CoverTabby is open, type a letter to focus Search and filter immediately without changing the selected style. Search must be enabled for the current mode. Press Enter to activate a result or Escape to cancel.

Win+Tab opens the optional desktop overview. Further Tab presses while holding Win select the next desktop; Shift+Tab selects the previous one. Hold Win to Keep Desktop Overview Open is enabled by default: releasing Win activates the selection. Disable it to leave the overview open; touchpad opening remains persistent. Beginning a rename leaves hold mode so typing is possible. Three quick three-finger taps toggle between windows and desktops while CoverTabby is open. A single tap is confirmed after a short 340 ms recognition window. Hover a desktop to reveal its centered name and Alt+Tab-style controls. Rename uses a blue pencil button, Delete uses a red trash button, and their labels expand on hover; Desktop 1 cannot be deleted. Rename supports Enter to save and Escape to cancel. The + button after the last desktop creates a new desktop; deleting a desktop moves its windows to the previous desktop. Desktop cards have equal sizes, stay flat and slide horizontally. Desktop overview always fills the monitor. Panels share Alt+Tab's theme-aware material and controls. Alt+Tab and Alt+` select the next/previous open app on the selected desktop; releasing Alt activates it. Left/right arrows select desktops, and clicking an app or pressing Enter focuses it. Minimized apps appear as an icon dock in a rounded top panel; titles appear only when hovering an icon. The app list follows the shell switcher visibility flag and refreshes while open, excluding retained hidden app windows. Live window captures are loaded incrementally for the selected and adjacent desktops (up to four extra captures, two in energy saver); unavailable frames use saved previews or icons and titles. Click or tap to activate the selected desktop; Escape or a downward swipe cancels. Each open HWND is shown as a separate fitted tile inside its desktop card; windows from the same application are never grouped or stacked together in this view.

Each card shows its wallpaper and window layout. Active-window content is live; other desktops reuse available snapshots. Windows without cached content show their application icon and title. At most three small wallpaper textures are loaded at once. Windows' internal desktop contracts vary between builds; unsupported builds show an availability message.

entry.title: Secondary Monitor Pin 1.1
entry.content:
Secondary Monitor Pin

Automatically pins windows that are placed on a secondary monitor so that they are shown on all virtual desktops, the same as choosing Show this window on all desktops from the window's title bar context menu.

When a window moves back to the primary monitor it is unpinned again, but only if this mod was the one that pinned it. Windows that were pinned manually are left untouched.

The mod runs as a tool mod in a dedicated process, so it does not inject into explorer.exe. It only talks to the virtual desktop manager when a window changes monitors, when a new window appears or when a window closes, which keeps the number of shell calls low and keeps switching virtual desktops smooth. A timer polls for monitor changes that the window event hooks do not report, such as Win+Shift+arrow, programmatic moves and display changes.

Windows that are on another virtual desktop are pinned too, so the secondary-monitor windows of every desktop end up shown together on all desktops.

Notes

  • Uses undocumented Windows virtual desktop interfaces, which may change with future Windows updates.
  • Works on Windows 10 and Windows 11.
  • Do not run this mod together with another tool that also pins windows across virtual desktops, as two implementations competing over the same shell interfaces can cause issues.

entry.title: Reopen Programs at Sign-in 2.0.1
entry.content:
• Fixed: nothing was reopened in Windhawk portable mode, because the mod storage drops line breaks. The saved list now uses a separator that survives (the old one is still read).
  • Fixed: programs with a background process but no window were treated as already open and skipped. The check now compares windows, also right before each launch.
  • Windhawk's own programs (tray app, 2.0 tool-mod hosts, editor) are no longer saved or reopened.
  • README: documents the already-open check and the helper-process limitation.

entry.title: AltTab Mouse Focus 1.1
entry.content:
AltTab Mouse Focus

Moves the mouse cursor to the center of the window that gets focused after switching windows with Alt+Tab.

  • Only acts on Alt+Tab. Clicking, other keyboard shortcuts or focus changes made by other programs do not move the cursor.
  • The cursor is moved once the Alt key is released, after the window switcher closes.
  • Ignores system overlays (desktop, taskbar, the Alt+Tab switcher).
  • Moves the cursor as soon as the selected window receives focus (EVENT_SYSTEM_FOREGROUND), instead of polling.
  • Works with multiple monitors: the cursor is centered on the monitor where the focused window is.

The mod runs as a tool mod in a dedicated process, so it does not inject into explorer.exe.

entry.title: Windows 7/8.1 UAC Recreation 1.0.0
entry.content:
Windows 7/8.1 UAC Recreation

This mod recreates the Windows 7 and 8.1 classic UAC interface on Windows 10 and 11. It changes only the presentation: Windows retains control of consent, authentication, and the secure desktop.

Features

  • Four themes: Windows 7 Basic, custom Aero, Windows 8.1, and Windows 10 (1507–1607).
  • It restores the native prompt if the recreation fails; never makes an elevation decision.
  • It leaves system files, settings, and credential prompts untouched.
  • It matches the banner and shield to Windows' publisher verdict.
  • Ithows the requesting program's icon and native prompt details when available.

Emergency shortcut

Press Ctrl+Shift+F10 to close the recreated dialog and return to the native prompt without approving or denying the request.

Themes

Windows 7 (Basic)

Windows 7 Aero

Windows 8.1

Windows 10 (1507–1607)

Installation

Windhawk excludes consent.exe by default. To enable the mod:

  1. Open Settings → Advanced settings → More advanced settings.
  2. Add consent.exe to the Process inclusion list.
  3. Install and enable the mod.

Without this change, the mod has no effect.

Settings

| Setting | Description | |---|---| | Dialog skin | Choose one of the four themes. | | Replace the UAC prompt | Replace the prompt or observe it and log events. | | Which apps get the Classic UAC prompt | Apply to all apps, only listed apps, or all except listed apps. | | App list | Semicolon-separated application names for the filter above. | | Button style | Use the system button or the mod's Aero-style button. | | Which shield is shown | Choose automatic, verified, question, or exclamation. | | Banner colour | Choose automatic, blue, yellow, or red; manual choices can only make the prompt more cautious. | | The Windows prompt, while the Windows 7 one is on screen | Move the native prompt off-screen or hide it. | | Read the elevation request | Read request details to show the app icon and "File origin". | | How long to wait for the prompt | Wait time, in milliseconds, before leaving the native prompt unchanged. | | Watchdog | Close the recreated dialog after this many seconds without a response. | | Panic hotkey | Shortcut to restore the native prompt; default: Ctrl+Shift+F10. | | Extra Yes/No key | Optional Alt+letter shortcut forwarded to the original prompt. | | Debug log | Record mod activity. | | Write a diagnostics dump | Write diagnostics; the mod runs in observation mode. | | Write the raw elevation request to the log | Log the raw request, which may include file and user names. | | How the prompt is found | Choose desktop watchers (recommended), polling, or hook only. |

Behavior and limitations

  • The banner follows the native publisher row. The shield follows the selected theme and Windows' verdict; the mod never upgrades an unknown or unverified publisher to verified.
  • Publisher checks use the file's Authenticode signature or its Windows catalog when applicable. The native verdict is not overridden.
  • Regedit is shown by its localized name only after Windows confirms the system file's signature.
  • Details that cannot be read from the native prompt are omitted, not guessed.
  • A XAML candidate without a Win32 edit control may be moved off-screen briefly during UI Automation classification.
  • Logs and diagnostic files can contain prompt text, command lines, file names, and user names. Enable them only when needed.

Tested systems

The modification has been tested on the following systems:

  • Windows 10 21H2
  • Windows 11 24H2
  • Windows 11 25H2

Credits

  • AdministratoX — Windows 11 24H2/25H2 testing
  • Microsoft — Documentation
  • m417z — Technical reference and review

Reporting issues

If there are anomalies, please report them to the author. It is recommended to include the debug log and, if needed, the diagnostic file.

entry.title: Tray Agenda 1.0.1
entry.content:
• Fixed the widget and popup text color when the Windows mode (taskbar) differs from the app mode: it now follows the taskbar's SystemUsesLightTheme setting, so the text stays readable on a dark taskbar with light apps and the other way around.
  • Added a "Contributing and issues" section to the mod description with the repository link.

entry.title: Sticky Notes: Alt+Tab group 1.1.1
entry.content:
Sticky Notes: Alt+Tab group

Keep multiple Microsoft Sticky Notes windows from filling the Alt+Tab switcher.

  • Show one representative Sticky Notes window in Alt+Tab.
  • Switch to Sticky Notes to bring all its open windows on the current virtual desktop forward together.
  • Minimized notes are restored; closed notes are not opened.
  • Switching from another application by clicking a note or its taskbar button also brings the open notes forward.
  • Use compact Sticky Notes previews, with a default maximum source size of 260 by 160 pixels while preserving the aspect ratio.
  • Other shell views that use the same thumbnail factory can also use this compact source size. The shell controls the final display scale.
  • Matching uses the note window's extended frame bounds.
  • Keep note contents, window sizes, positions, and ownership unchanged.

Compatibility

  • Windows 11, x64, with the standard XAML Alt+Tab switcher.
  • Locally tested on Windows 11 25H2, build 26200.9457, Windhawk 1.7.3, and Microsoft Sticky Notes 6.1.4.0.
  • Other Windows builds and the newer OneNote-based Sticky Notes experience have not been tested.
  • Uses private shell symbols, which may change after Windows updates.
  • Tested alongside Alt+Tab per monitor 1.2 with its cursor-monitor filter.
  • That mod's monitor filtering still applies. Notes restored after selection can be on any monitor on the current virtual desktop.
  • Disabling this mod restores the normal switcher behavior.
  • Do not enable both a local copy and the catalog version simultaneously.

Settings

  • Preview maximum width / height: maximum reported Sticky Notes thumbnail source dimensions. Values at or below zero use the defaults (260 / 160).

Credits

The Alt+Tab visibility-filtering approach is adapted from Alt+Tab per monitor by L3r0y and Alt+Tab: Hide ghost windows by David Trapp (CherryDT). Their MIT notices are retained below.

entry.title: Shake to Find Cursor 1.4.1
entry.content:
• Fixed flickering and stutter with larger pointer sizes (Settings > Accessibility > Mouse pointer and touch > Size). Thanks to @winchestercanal for tracking this down in #5595.
  • Fixed the cursor briefly appearing at the wrong size when it changes type (e.g. arrow to text cursor) during or after the animation.
  • Fixed the cursor not updating while the mouse is held still.

entry.title: Cursor auto-hide on idle 1.1
entry.content:
• Added the Toggle hotkey setting: a global shortcut that turns the auto-hide on and off at runtime.
  • Added Record the shortcut by pressing it: press the shortcut within 60 seconds and it is copied to the clipboard in the format the field expects, with an on-screen note while the window is open.
  • A shortcut needs Ctrl, Alt or Win, because a global shortcut takes its key away from every application; F1 to F24, Pause and ScrollLock may be used alone or with Shift.
  • Recording accepts every key the field can hold, punctuation, lock keys and numeric keypad included, and the note is placed on the monitor under the pointer at that monitor's scale.
  • Documented the recording order - shortcut first, then paste - in the readme and in both settings descriptions.

entry.title: Tourne'Table [Audio Visualizer] 2.1.0
entry.content:
• Precision analysis engine: every bar is its own band (real-input FFT, three resolution tiers; log, mel, bark, ERB, fractional-octave or note layouts; A/C/Z weighting; time-based ballistics). The 1.x analysis stays as Analysis Engine = Classic.
  • Direct3D 11 renderer: instanced bars drawn from a buffer. It skips frames that didn't change. Direct2D stays as an option and as the fallback.
  • Idle: one wake per frame while playing. In silence it wakes only on audio. Deep Idle then stops the loopback stream and reads the peak meter instead.
  • Right-click menu for live quick settings, stored in mod values and laid over the settings page.
  • Any audio device as the source, outputs or inputs.
  • New shapes and styles: Terminal, Goniometer, LED Meter, Spectrogram, VU Needles and more. Reflection, Glow and Bloom, and bar modifiers.
  • Media Card and My Styles with a Style Editor.
  • Placement: Taskbar, Panel and Dock To App.
  • Setup sharing: codes and .ttstyle files. A Community button reads a list of shared styles from GitHub, but only when it's pressed.
  • 32-bit: builds for 32-bit as well as 64-bit.
  • Readme: the images now load from the Tourne-Style repo.

entry.title: Mac Island & Dock 2.0.1
entry.content:
Panels and look

  • Panels always open under the island (over it on the lower half of the screen), under the item clicked, the same for every panel (#6211). A panel already open for another item (the volume's page, then Wi-Fi) moves under the new one, and a closing panel no longer takes clicks meant for what's under it.
  • Every icon on the pill is the same size (the media and control center buttons and the arrows were smaller, the apps' icons bigger), and a new "Icon size" option (70% to 150%, per profile and monitor, in every style) changes them apart from the island's size, so a big bar can keep small icons.
  • Notches grow with their items until they almost touch each other (they scroll only then), instead of each stopping at a third of the screen; the "Icons before scrolling" option now says it's for the other apps' tray icons.
  • The power menu's confirmation shows its whole text, and buttons and menu rows no longer end with "…".
  • The control center's pages opened straight from their pill icon (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth…) have no back arrow (nothing to go back to).
  • A panel opened and closed again at once (a quick double click) no longer leaves its outline behind the island.

Profiles and monitors

  • The profiles' button is per profile: turning it off on one monitor's island no longer turns it off on the others.
  • A monitor with its own profile no longer follows the main island for options added after its profile was saved (they're kept in its profile as it first shows them).
  • A monitor with its own profile shows the virtual desktops, the keyboard language, USB drives and the microphone/camera/location in use when its profile turns them on, even with the main island's off.

Notifications

  • The Widgets button's news show on the island as "Widgets" with its icon, and a click opens Widgets (it was an unnamed grey square that did nothing) (#6206).
  • Windows' own notifications (like Windows Security's "Update antivirus protection", or a sender whose icon is only in the registry) show their name and icon instead of "SecurityCenter" and a grey square (#6206, #6187); apps whose windows carry no app ID (like Discord) show their program's icon.
  • A switch for the icons of the apps with notifications on the pill (Notifications section, on by default).
  • Clearing notifications on the island (the X, a swipe, a card's button, "Clear all") also removes them from Windows' notification center; "Clear all" removes only the ones the island's list shows (compared by ID).
  • With the island's own notifications, a priority app's Windows banner no longer flashes before the pill takes it, and a notification right after a screenshot shows in the pill (#6159).
  • With the island's own notifications and its "Do not disturb" on, Windows' "Do not disturb" is "alarms only": an app on Windows' priority list (like the Snipping Tool) no longer shows Windows' banner or plays its sound (calls, alarms and reminders still show and ring in the pill). Windows' "Do not disturb" is also turned back off when the mod is turned off or removed while the island isn't running.
  • The keyboard language bubble only shows when the mode changes in the same app (not when opening Start or minimizing an app), once, over the island's line, without repeating "中" (#6210, #6199, #6233).

Control center

  • Brightness with more monitors: a slider for each monitor (with its name) instead of one for all, and the wheel on an island's brightness item changes its own monitor only (the control center follows it). The list is read again when a monitor is plugged in or out, a monitor plugged back in shows once it answers, and one turned off (still connected) leaves the list the next time it opens.
  • Bluetooth: clicking headphones or speakers connects or disconnects them, showing "Connecting…", then "Connected" or "Couldn't connect" on their row, and connected ones have a "Disconnect" button; other devices open Windows' Bluetooth settings (#6160). A control that's on shows in the island's own colors on the pill (no colored icon).
  • The volume mixer shows each app once, like Windows' mixer: an app playing from more than one of its processes (Spotify during an ad) was listed twice.
  • Updates: an app updated in the terminal that only finishes when it closes (like VS Code while open) says "Close it to finish" instead of offering the update again.

Folders

  • Pinned folders can be dragged into another order; each folder's items can be listed by name or newest first (its own order) and searched (a name or a type like *.pdf); the folders shown update by themselves while the panel is open (a download, a file renamed or deleted), their rows come in with a short animation, and going back slides the columns.
  • Files and folders can be dragged out to Explorer or the desktop, copied or moved as chosen (asked the first time, with "Remember my choice"; also in the island's settings), and files can be dropped on a folder in the panel, from the panel itself or from Explorer and the desktop (held a moment on the folders item, the panel opens; held on a folder, it opens), copied or moved by Windows as in Explorer (its questions for names already there, its progress, Ctrl+Z). After a drop the panel stays open, the folder opens and the files dropped light up.

New pill items

  • komorebi's layout (an option, off by default): the current layout of the island's monitor as an icon and a name ("Grid", "Paused", "Monocle"), after a dot for each of its workspaces (the one shown lit, ones with windows faint, empty ones a ring or hidden by an option, like yasb's; a click shows another one), only while komorebi runs; its click opens a menu with the layouts' icons to change the layout, tiling, monocle and pause for that monitor (#6163). It follows komorebi's own events (komorebic subscribe-pipe), with nothing polled, and finds a komorebi that starts slowly (at sign-in). komorebi's start and stop button has its own icon, and the settings say when "with whkd" is on but whkd isn't installed.
  • The app in focus on each monitor's island (an option, off by default): its icon and name (as the taskbar shows them, Steam included), or "Desktop", sliding to the next one; a click brings it to the front.

Other fixes

  • Fog shows as a cloud in the weather (Windows 11's fog emoji is a plain square) (#6226).
  • Changing the wallpaper: the transition stays until Windows really shows the new picture (the old one no longer flashes back, and Windows' own zoom no longer shows through), the picture is placed exactly where Windows puts it ("Fill" keeps a third of what's cut above and two thirds below, measured on Windows 11; "Span" set for one monitor is drawn like "Fill"), so it no longer slides down at the end, and the transition no longer covers the taskbar of a monitor showing the desktop.
  • Clicking what's playing's cover brings back an app hidden in the tray that ignores its tray icon's click (Spotify from the Microsoft Store): it's started again by its ID, which shows its window.
  • Dock: one shown for an app's notification on one monitor no longer moves another monitor's dock (with monitors at different scales, the second dock was left almost hidden), and its background tint applies when Windows can't blur (transparency effects off, energy saver) instead of turning solid (#6251).
  • A transparent taskbar hides again while an app's button was already asking for attention when the taskbar's style changed.

entry.title: Toggle Hidden Files 1.1.0
entry.content:
• Added separate and configurable modifier to toggle protected operating system files
  • Fixed a bug where icons may occasionally disappear in File Explorer when toggling back the hidden files and folders.

entry.title: What When Where Notes 1.3.2
entry.content:
What When Where Notes

A customizable desktop note overlay for Windows, powered by Windhawk. Organize reminders in three editable parts: What - When - Where.

Screenshots

Task overview and status indicators

Custom colors and row highlighting

Edit notes directly on the desktop

Right-click color and transparency menu

Task status indicators

Click the colored circle next to a task to change its state:

  • ⚪ Gray — Open: The task has not been started.
  • 🔴 Red — In Progress: Work on the task is underway.
  • 🟢 Green — Completed: What, When and Where are struck through.

Cycle: ⚪ Open → 🔴 In Progress → 🟢 Completed → ⚪ Open. Each task's status is saved across Windhawk restarts.

Features

  • Up to 14 numbered note rows with independently editable What, When and Where fields.
  • Optional centered title, adjustable fonts, spacing and colors.
  • Three status states for each row: gray (open), red (in progress), and green (done). Completed notes are struck through.
  • Add rows, remove the last row, or delete a selected row.
  • Move the overlay with a configurable drag-mode hotkey.
  • Adjustable transparency and note color; optional always-on-top behavior.
  • Saved notes, row statuses, position and display preferences persist across restarts.

Using the notes

  • Click a What, When or Where field to edit it. Press Enter to save or Esc to cancel. Leaving the edit field also saves.
  • Click + to add a row (up to the configured maximum) or - to remove the last row.
  • Click the X next to a row to delete that row. At least one row is kept.
  • Click a status circle to cycle through open, in progress and done.
  • Right-click the overlay to open the color and transparency menu.
  • Mouse wheel over the overlay to scale it in 10% steps (20% to 320%); middle-click to reset the scale.
  • Press Ctrl+Alt+N by default to toggle drag mode, then drag the overlay with the left mouse button. Press the hotkey again to exit drag mode.

Configuration

Open Settings to customize the initial position, always-on-top mode, title, the three default note fields, separators, maximum row count, fonts, colors, default transparency, default scale, and the drag hotkey.

Note: Existing edited notes and saved display preferences are stored separately from the initial defaults. Changing a default does not automatically overwrite previously saved note rows. A previously dragged position is preserved when changing unrelated options. Editing X/Y settings explicitly moves the overlay to those new coordinates.

Technical information

  • Designed for Windows / Windhawk.
  • Runs as a Windhawk tool mod, using a dedicated windhawk.exe helper process.
  • The overlay is implemented with the Windows API and GDI.
  • Source code and license: GitHub repository.

Project background and relation to Easy Notes

This mod is an independent Windows/Windhawk implementation inspired by the original ToDoLite / What When Where Rainmeter project by the same author: https://forum.rainmeter.net/viewtopic.php?t=42543#p215957

Unlike free-form desktop sticky notes, this mod displays a structured three-field task list (What / When / Where) with distinct Open / In Progress / Completed states. The current version is intentionally focused on that workflow.

Author

SilverAmd

entry.title: Explorer Properties Button 1.0.0
entry.content:
Explorer Properties Button

Adds a Properties button to the Windows 11 File Explorer command bar, between the Delete and Sort buttons. Clicking it opens the properties dialog of the current selection:

  • Multiple selection - opens the combined properties dialog, just like the context menu's Properties entry.
  • Virtual locations - This PC, Recycle Bin, Quick Access and other items without a filesystem path work too.
  • No selection (configurable) - shows the properties of the current folder, or does nothing.

The dialog opens via fast shell APIs (SHObjectProperties / SHMultiFileProperties) without building the shell context menu, so it appears without the delay that loading shell extensions would add. The context-menu properties verb is only used as a fallback for exotic locations.

System requirements

Windows 11 24H2 / 25H2 or newer, with the WinAppSDK (WinUI 3) File Explorer command bar. Older versions (Windows 10, Windows 11 23H2 and earlier) use a completely different command bar; the mod stays silently disabled there.

How it works

The mod hooks a couple of functions of File Explorer's own WinUI 3 code (FileExplorerExtensions.dll), gets the command bar from there, and inserts a WinRT-constructed AppBarButton into its PrimaryCommands. The button survives tab switches, navigation and new windows, and is cleanly removed when the mod is disabled. Clicks drive the shell lookups from a worker thread, so the Explorer UI stays responsive.

File Explorer windows which were already open when the mod is enabled are handled too, but if the button doesn't show up in one of them right away, opening a new tab or navigating to another folder makes it appear.

Implementation follows the Explorer Command Bar mod by DanRotaru from the official windhawk-mods repository.

资源管理器属性按钮（中文说明）

在 Windows 11 文件资源管理器的命令栏（工具栏）上，"删除"和"排序"按钮之间添加一个"属性"按钮，点击后打开当前选中项目的属性对话框：

  • 支持多选：多选时与右键菜单里的"属性"一样，打开合并的属性对话框。
  • 支持虚拟位置：此电脑、回收站、Quick Access 等没有文件系统路径的项目也能正确打开属性。
  • 没有选中项时（可配置）：显示当前文件夹的属性，或什么都不做。

属性对话框通过快速 Shell API（SHObjectProperties / SHMultiFileProperties）直接打开，不构建右键菜单，避免了加载 shell 扩展带来的延迟；右键菜单的"属性"动词仅作为特殊位置的兜底。

系统要求

适用于 Windows 11 24H2 / 25H2 及以上使用 WinAppSDK (WinUI 3) 命令栏的文件资源管理器。旧版本（Windows 10、Windows 11 23H2 及更早）使用完全不同的命令栏实现，本 mod 会在其中安静地保持不启用状态。

工作原理

本 mod hook 了文件资源管理器自身的 WinUI 3 代码（FileExplorerExtensions.dll）中的若干函数，从那里拿到命令栏，并把一个用 WinRT 构造的 AppBarButton 插入 PrimaryCommands；按钮在切换标签页、导航、新窗口后自动恢复，禁用 mod 时被干净移除。点击的 Shell 查询由独立工作线程驱动，资源管理器界面保持响应。

启用本 mod 时已经打开的文件资源管理器窗口也会被处理；若某个已有窗口中按钮没有立即出现，打开一个新标签页或导航到其他文件夹即可让它出现。

实现参考了官方仓库的 Explorer Command Bar mod（DanRotaru），在此致谢。

entry.title: Win+V Panel Tweaks 1.0.0
entry.content:
Win+V Panel Tweaks

The Win+V clipboard panel and the Win+. emoji panel are the same panel, with tabs for Most recently used, Emoji, GIF, Kaomoji, Symbols and Clipboard. This mod makes the panel bigger or smaller and hides the tabs you turn off in its settings.

Panel size

The panel is normally 360 x 400 (in display-scaled pixels). Width and height are scaled separately, e.g. width 150% and height 100% gives 540 x 400. Windows still keeps the panel within the space available on screen. A new size applies the next time the panel opens.

By default the items keep their normal size, so a taller panel shows more clipboard entries and a wider one fits more emoji per row. Turn on "Scale content with the panel" to have the items grow with the panel instead.

Tabs

The Clipboard tab is always kept. Hiding a tab only removes its button: a shortcut that opens a view directly still opens it (e.g. Win+. still opens Emoji even when the Emoji tab is hidden).

How it works

The panel is drawn by TextInputHost.exe. Its size is computed in InputApp.dll, which the mod hooks using Microsoft's public symbols, so the first start after installing may take a moment while Windhawk downloads them.

The tab strip lives in a web page hosted in a WebView inside the panel. The same hook finds that WebView each time the panel opens and runs a small script in the page, which marks the chosen tabs as hidden in the page's own view model, re-applying it whenever the page resets them. Tweaks therefore show up the next time the panel opens after the mod is enabled.

That page ships with Windows but Microsoft can update it separately. If it changes in a way the mod doesn't recognize, the mod leaves it alone and the panel keeps working as usual.

Tested on Windows 11 25H2 (build 26200).

Source and research notes: https://github.com/jayll1303/WindowsClipboardMods
